title: Your target market isn't demographic: define it by shared needs and use-cases, not size or geography
summary: Jason argues that demographics and firmographics (company size, geography, age) usually misdescribe a market. Using WP Engine, where Google and big banks bought "SMB" hosting, he shows the real target is people who share needs and reasons for buying. He gives the testimonial test and a long list of better segmentation dimensions.

principles.text: Define your target market by what customers value and the use-case they have, not demographics or firmographics.
principles.quote: Rather, the target market depends on the use-cases and characteristics of the users.

principles.text: Large companies buying your small-business product is not a signal to go up-market; individual teams buy too, for the same reasons.
principles.quote: The reason is that _individual teams_ at large companies also buy things.

principles.text: WP Engine's target was people who valued enterprise-grade quality, open-source flexibility, and mid-priced hosting, not 'small businesses with WordPress'.
principles.quote: This happened because our target market wasn't "small businesses and individuals with WordPress."

principles.text: Keep asking 'why do they value that?' to find the common threads, then write specific positioning like 'Enterprise-Grade WordPress'.
principles.quote: You can find more pieces of that definition by continuing to ask "why do they value those things?"

principles.text: Testimonial test: profile B is in your market if they'd be swayed by an effusive testimonial from existing customer A.
principles.quote: Would customer [B] be swayed by a genuine, effusive testimonial given by [A]?

principles.text: Derive the target market from your best customers (high retention, upgrades, 10 NPS, advocates) and their shared characteristics.
principles.quote: Your target market is the set of potential customers that your best customers self-identify with, in the sense that they would view each other's testimonials as compelling.
